implemented: When an unpublished bootstrap fails with its private root already closed and borrowed caller still connected, make one owned cleanup-channel attempt using the exact caller configuration, hostname, endpoint and event bus.
Reuse existing auxiliary authentication, original-key reservations and binding. Send session LOGOFF only after obtaining a verified new channel key.
Preserve the original authentication failure; attach cleanup failures as suppressed exceptions. Close and release both owned transports while preserving borrowed-session work.

native_fault_assertions: Corrupted final reply: genuine peer MAC verifies before input corruption; original-key LOGOFF uses reserved MID 3.
Dropped successful final input with live root: authentication waits while older open remains usable; reserved original-key LOGOFF succeeds.
Dropped successful final input and closed root: a fresh owned channel binds with distinct original-key request MIDs; cleanup LOGOFF uses a different actual channel key and receives success.
Cleanup connect failure: exactly one candidate is created then closed; injected failure is suppressed on the original IOException; no LOGOFF succeeds and remote cleanup is unconfirmed.
Every failure case preserves the borrowed caller and older open, empties provisional authentication state and permits fresh authentication retry.
audit_scope: New failure cases check actual key roles, distinct binding request MIDs, successful peer LOGOFF responses where available and lifecycle behavior. They are not a new independent full-wire nonce audit. Existing two public wire-audited profiles retain their separate bounded scope.
